_doc: #1471 Infra > APIs: the third-party API providers the fleet uses, declared here and nowhere else (build.json declares the row and its pages, Kotlin spells none of it). A provider's `group` is one of `groups[].id`; a group's `page` is the Infra page id build.json declares for it. `secrets` holds secret NAMES only (an env var or a vault / store key), never a value: test/test-c3-declarative.sh D6 rejects any other key, a name that does not look like a name, and anything token-shaped. `used_by` names fleet apps (ids of the Android constellation) and containers (names in containers_declared.json) where the data or the registry has them.
_doc_mcp_catalogue: #1725 Infra > APIs > C3 MCP: the MCP servers of the C3 environment with every tool and the c3-api route it maps to. They were listed by Cloud C3 Webserver > API (its MCP page and the remote nodes of its Topology), which shows only the phone now and keeps the tools that act on the device. The next line is GENERATED by data/gen_c3_mcp.py from ac_cloud-c3-webserver/data/mcp-catalogue.json minus the device tools of data/fleet/device-access.json (do not edit it; run the script's write); `group` is the id of the group above whose page draws it. Names and addresses only, never a secret.
_doc_fleet_endpoints: #1718 Infra > APIs > C3 Endpoints: the fleet services of the C3 environment (the other machines), each with its public URL and its mesh URL. They were listed by Cloud C3 Webserver > API (Public Endpoints, and the fleet group of Mesh Endpoints), which shows only the phone now. The next line is GENERATED by data/gen_fleet_endpoints.py from ac_cloud-account/build.json::fleet_endpoints.services (do not edit it; run the script's write); `group` is the id of the group above whose page draws it. It carries addresses and names only, never a secret.
